content: In young individuals with Type 1 Diabetes, nephropathy and retinopathy are significant complications that require careful management. For the treatment of nephropathy, the use of an ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor or an angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) is recommended when the albumin-to-creatinine ratio surpasses 30 mg/g. This diagnosis should be confirmed by observing elevated levels in at least two out of three urine samples collected over a six-month period. However, due to the teratogenic effects of these medications, individuals of childbearing potential must avoid using ACE inhibitors or ARBs unless they are employing reliable methods of contraception to prevent pregnancy.
